description: Population measurements filed by pm items, enforced as ceilings (pm-ips23h). Each declaration names the item that owns the defect, a selector that recomputes the population from tracked data, and the count that was filed. A ceiling retires automatically when its owner reaches a terminal status.

declarations.note: blocks rows are resolved by pm graph but invisible to the readiness resolver behind pm next, so an item gated only by a blocks row is classified ready. The owning item measured 219; the population had already grown to 241 before anything could fail on it.

related_to is stored verbatim and folded into related only at read time, so a jq or grep pipeline over the store selects the wrong token. The owning item measured 16; the alias population it exists to retire had grown to 43.
Active items unreachable from the relationship graph. Held at zero since the typed-connectivity work landed; this declaration keeps it there.
Active items reachable by at most one edge, which is the shape a spine-only lineage leaves behind. Held at zero; a new item filed without typed relationships fails here.
Two known pairs, each two genuine defects sharing one upstream issue code. The fix is check-side; neither pair may be renamed or merged. The ceiling stops a third pair appearing unnoticed.
Linked file paths that no longer exist, dominated by generated artifacts. The owning fix refuses such links at write time; until it lands the population may not grow.
A tracked path with no live owner remains in the linked-resource cleanup lineage and may not multiply.
Historical terminal items missing close reasons remain owned by the evidence-preserving metadata backfill and may only shrink.
Closed items missing the resolution triple. Every close from here on must carry it, so this ceiling only ever falls.
A pending local delivery queue remains an explicit observability limitation; an error status is a regression.
